title: Circus Sideshow (Parade de cirque)
story_hook: Seurat's most mysterious major canvas — its hypnotic nocturnal circus crowd baffled critics at the 1888 Salon; scholars have debated its "most geometric, most mysterious" symbolism for over a century

title: Aristotle with a Bust of Homer
story_hook: Commissioned for a mystery subject by a Sicilian nobleman in 1653; sold multiple times; purchased by the Met in 1961 for a then-record $2.3 million — the first artwork to break the million-dollar auction barrier
yt_coverage: no dedicated Short found; several long-form docs (MET 150, conservator behind-the-scenes)

title: View of Toledo
story_hook: Only surviving pure landscape by El Greco; painted in defiance of a suspected Council of Trent ban on landscapes; the city geography is deliberately distorted — historians debate whether it is a spiritual vision or a coded protest
yt_coverage: 1 dedicated Short (Art Shorts #149); several long-form docs

title: Madame X (Virginie Amélie Avegno Gautreau)
story_hook: Sargent painted Gautreau's dress strap slipping off her shoulder — the original scandalous version of the 1884 Paris Salon; he later repainted it, erasing the evidence of the most notorious moment in 19th-century portraiture.
yt_coverage: 1 dedicated Short found (scandal angle); no long-form dedicated video; podcast episode (ArtCurious S4E1); high opportunity
longform_angle: Sargent's original painted version had the strap slipping — evidence he physically repainted over it to escape scandal; the original strap-down pose survives only in preparatory sketches, raising the question: what exactly did Paris see that night in 1884?

title: The Musicians
story_hook: X-ray analysis revealed Caravaggio painted over a hidden original scene; one figure may be a self-portrait; the painting disappeared for centuries and resurfaced in 1952 in damaged condition — Caravaggio's most intimate and debated early work.
yt_coverage: no dedicated long-form YouTube video found; only article/blog content; very low YouTube coverage
longform_angle: X-ray in 1997 revealed Caravaggio painted over a hidden original scene between the musicians — what was he hiding, and why does the painting's self-portrait figure stare directly at us from beneath centuries of overpaint?

title: The Denial of Saint Peter
story_hook: Painted in the final weeks of Caravaggio's life while he was a fugitive with a papal death sentence; scholars debate whether this was a confession of his own betrayal or a last bid for papal pardon — he died before it could be delivered.
yt_coverage: 1 dedicated YouTube video (Kelly Bagdanov, 2020); no dedicated Short; low coverage for long-form
longform_angle: Caravaggio painted this as a fugitive days before his mysterious death in 1610 — was it a coded confession to the Pope, or proof he never expected to survive long enough to deliver it?

title: The Gulf Stream
story_hook: Homer secretly reworked the canvas years after its 1899 debut — adding a distant ship, altering the boat — but refused to explain the racial politics his critics could not ignore; when asked about the Black man's fate, he replied only with sarcasm.
yt_coverage: 2 Met-official Shorts; 1 MetSpeaks long-form lecture; 1 educational homeschool video; medium coverage — no dedicated narrative long-form Short from storytelling channel
longform_angle: Homer secretly modified the painting between 1900 and 1906 — adding a rescue ship on the horizon — but never admitted why; the hidden rework raises the question of whether he was responding to critics who saw racial abandonment, not maritime drama.

title: Mäda Primavesi (1903–2000)
story_hook: Klimt spent 200 sessions sketching a 9-year-old girl and wrote in her autograph book "The day is like night unless I see you" — his only major child portrait; Mäda lived until 2000 and became the last surviving subject of a Klimt masterwork, outliving the man who painted her by 88 years.
yt_coverage: no dedicated YouTube video or Short found; virtually no video coverage — high opportunity
longform_angle: Klimt wrote to a 9-year-old girl "The day is like night unless I see you" — 200 sketches, a family that later went bankrupt and was forced to sell her portrait; Mäda survived to 2000 as the last living Klimt subject and had to watch her own face hang in a museum without her.
